title: Decoding Ultramarathon: Muscle Damage as the Main Impediment to Performance
population: Current Opinion on ultramarathon physiology (events 50 to 5000 km); no new participants
findings: Authors argue that muscle damage and associated fatigue is the main impediment to performance in long ultramarathons, more performance-limiting than aerobic capacity, running economy or gastrointestinal distress.

They propose a lab protocol of downhill running with pre- to post-exercise contractile measures (electrical or magnetic stimulation of the quadriceps or central nerves), muscle damage biomarkers (CK, LDH, myoglobin) and muscle imaging.
They close with training and racing advice on mitigating the deleterious effects of muscle damage; the abstract gives no recovery-duration numbers.
limitations: Expert opinion without new data; abstract only (full text not read); about performance limitation during races, not post-race recovery; year is the print year (Sports Med 2025;55), online 2024-10-15.
implications: Gives a rationale, by extrapolation, for basing the post-race hold and return on muscle-damage recovery (impact load, downhill, repeated loading) and not on aerobic or cardiovascular signals, which is why HRV and resting HR can only be advisory.
Not a source of numbers: do not cite for any day count or fraction.

verification.notes: Crossref (online 2024-10-15, Tiller and Millet) and Europe PMC abstract (PMID 39405022, Review, pubYear 2025) re-read. Second author is Millet GY (Guillaume), corrected from GP. Added the limitation that the paper concerns in-race performance, not post-race recovery.
